text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- There are a lot of jobs available in Norway. The health and child care sectors, schools, construction and other industries are short of workers.
- Sweden's TV4, which has some of Europe's highest advertising costs, will reduce its fees from January 1.

- Managing director of chocolate company Cloetta Lennart Bohlin says the Swedish chocolate market is continuing to grow -- by three to four percent in October and November, which is clearly better than normal.
- Demand is high in Europe for top managers, especially within the information technology sector.
- Telecoms group Ericsson is frantically trying to get its next generation mobile telephone, which can operate on two frequencies, to the market.
- Sweden's Metall union will give its members who have been unemployed for more than three months a Christmas present -- payment of 200 crowns and a half kilogram of coffee.
- Volvo would like to change its bonus system for users of company cars, saying rewards are ending up in the pockets of the drivers instead of their employers who pay for the cars.
- Swedbank is one of the bidders for the state's 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek, the head of the bank's board Goran Collert says.

- Skandia's board head Sven Soderberg says about its plans to merge with Stadshypotek that it was an opportunity that the company could not miss and Finance Minister Erik Asbrik did not realise they were serious about the proposal.
- Family clothing company Hollywood shows some of the industry's most impressive sales figures.
